segments.t: Out on the night streets of Sineozersk. Last time, Ilona brought Arkady a pillow, a blanket, and vodka, told him she had deleted the video of Samson, and joined Arkady's campaign to turn Samson into a people's hero. Meanwhile, Samson and Nina are speeding through town in the test-drive car to return it before ten o'clock. We'll hear it in Russian first; don't worry about catching every word.
Нам надо сдать машину до десяти часов.
И мне сейчас нельзя ехать медленно.
Иначе все поймут, что за рулём пьяный!
Let's take the scene line by line. Samson is flying down the night street, and Nina holds on tight.
'Samson, you're driving very fast!' Russian has a special verb for going by vehicle rather than on foot, and this is its 'you' form. Nina has had a few glasses of sparkling wine at dinner.
'My head is spinning already.' Literally, 'at me already the head is turning round'. Samson has his eye on the clock.
Нам надо сдать машину до десяти часов.

'We have to return the car before ten o'clock.' The dealership manager lent him the luxury car only until ten in the evening. After the preposition 'before', both 'ten' and 'hours' take the 'of' case. And Samson is proud of his new title.
'I am, for your information, the people's candidate!' The two words in the middle mean 'by the way' or 'for your information'. He adds a rule.
'The people's candidate isn't late, got it?' In Russian, 'to be late' is a single verb, not an adjective. And then comes Samson's logic.
И мне сейчас нельзя ехать медленно.
'And I mustn't drive slowly right now.' Literally, 'to me right now it is forbidden to drive slowly'. Why not?
Иначе все поймут, что за рулём пьяный!
'Otherwise everyone will realise the driver is drunk!' Literally, 'that behind the steering wheel is a drunk man'. Tipsy Nina finds this argument completely convincing.
'True. Go faster, Samson!' The word for 'faster' is the comparative form of 'fast'. Suddenly Samson spots flashing lights ahead.
'Quiet, quiet! I see the police!' The noun for 'police' changes its '-ya' ending to '-yu' as the direct object. Samson isn't worried.
'Now we'll get away from them.' Adding the prefix 'u-' to the verb for driving means 'to drive away'. He turns into the dark courtyards behind the Society of the Blind.
'I know this town really well!' In the show he says he knows the town like his own five fingers. Nina is thrilled by the ride.
'Samson, I love you so much!' After all their quarrels, this evening out has made her happy again. Samson grins.
'And I love you too! Look!' Right ahead of them is a loading ramp in front of the glass wall of the car dealership.

'We're flying! Hop!' The car launches off the ramp and crashes straight through the showroom window, landing inside right on time at ten o'clock. Now let's listen to the whole ride once more, start to finish.
Нам надо сдать машину до десяти часов.
И мне сейчас нельзя ехать медленно.
Иначе все поймут, что за рулём пьяный!
So the people's candidate delivers the test-drive car before ten o'clock — right through the dealership window. One short scene in Moscow remains to finish the episode; see you there.

lines.fragment: все поймут, что за рулем пьяный
